rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Grants exactly one wall-assisted jump per airborne cycle. After leaving legitimate ground, a fresh Space press first checks whether Wall Jump is unused and the actor's movement hull is within WallJumpProbeDistance = 24 world units of a valid static blocking wall surface. A valid wall surface is approximately vertical, physically reachable by a short hull/trace test from the actor without crossing blocking geometry, and belongs to world/generated architecture rather than another actor, a movable physics prop, or a cosmetic/nonblocking surface. If several walls qualify, use the nearest valid surface; deterministic trace order/stable surface identity breaks an exact tie. When valid, the press consumes the one Wall Jump for that airborne cycle, applies the actor's ordinary voluntary-jump vertical takeoff impulse, and adds a bounded horizontal kick directly away from the contacted wall normal. A wall contact by itself never resets Wall Jump or Cloud Step, so repeated wall climbing/bouncing cannot create unlimited jumps. Input priority while airborne is WALL JUMP > CLOUD STEP > FLOAT ON: if a valid unused Wall Jump exists on a fresh Space press, it fires instead of Cloud Step; if no Wall Jump is currently eligible, Cloud Step may consume that press under its own rules; Float On is the lowest-priority hold-at-apex behavior and never intercepts a fresh Space press that can legally produce Wall Jump or Cloud Step. Spring Heel may increase Wall Jump's vertical apex under its ordinary voluntary-jump rule but does not amplify the lateral kick. rows.effect: Define HeroOfLegendHPThreshold = min(100, MaxHP). Whenever the actor commits a legitimate Crowbar/Long-Sword-family primary swing while CurrentHP >= HeroOfLegendHPThreshold, that swing also emits exactly one Hero of Legend pulse. The pulse is a bright laser-energy duplicate shaped to match the equipped Crowbar/Long-Sword-family weapon itself rather than a generic bolt, projected forward in the swing/aim direction, and the emission produces one distinct shrill piercing 3D sound with ordinary world attenuation. If the hit has no other authored physical push, the proc creates a push-tagged RequestedPushDistance of 168 world units and therefore resolves as a normal single-tag Push save. If the hit already has an authored physical push, add +168 world units to that event's RequestedPushDistance before compatible multipliers and retain both independent Push-tag sources for the shared save. Thus Shotgun's inherent Push tag plus a successful Pusher-family proc produces PushTagMultiplicity = 2: there is still only one combined push and one logical PushSave event, but the defender rolls that PushSave with disadvantage under the universal duplicate save-bearing effect-tag rule. Higher Pusher-family ranks replace lower ranks and therefore remain one Pusher-family tag source rather than creating multiple copies merely from rank ownership. The completed request then resolves through the shared STR-based push save before LOD.Pushback collision/movement resolution. On failure, a pre-existing push still resolves normally. While that cooldown is active for the same attacker-target pair, later hits make no Pusher-family proc roll, although any authored push on those hits still resolves normally. A successful Pusher-family proc starts the 0.50-second cooldown; a failed eligible roll does not. Different targets track cooldown independently. rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, Magic-using AI
rows.effect: Sets ManaBarrierFeatDiversionFraction = 0.15. This feat family is unavailable to Wizard-class actors; it is the INT-gated HP→Magic diversion path for eligible non-Wizards. For an eligible non-Wizard with Mana Barrier, Mana Barrier grants ArcaneShieldCapability and HPToMagicDiversionFraction = ManaBarrierFeatDiversionFraction = 0.15 while Arcane Shield is online; while shattered, effective HPToMagicDiversionFraction = 0 until the shared 5d6! shatter timer clears. After an incoming damage event has completed all ordinary damage resolution, including attack dice/Boomchains, weakness/resistance/immunity handling, CON DamageResistancePerDie, and other authored mitigation or amplification, but immediately before HP is removed, define ResolvedHPDamage as the HP damage that would otherwise be applied; it may be fractional. DesiredHPDiversion = ResolvedHPDamage × HPToMagicDiversionFraction. ActualHPDiversion = min(DesiredHPDiversion, CurrentMagic). MagicSpent = ActualHPDiversion and FinalHPDamage = ResolvedHPDamage - ActualHPDiversion. Fractional HP diversion and fractional Magic damage are legal. Magic cannot fall below 0. This diversion authority applies to ordinary damage events from actors or the environment, including damage to temporary Tetris overfill, but not direct kill commands, non-damage death states, or effects explicitly tagged ignoreManaBarrier. HP-to-Magic diversion loss is classified as Magic damage, not voluntary Magic spending, so spend/cast triggers do not fire merely because the barrier absorbed damage. If the barrier reduces Magic to 0, normal zero-Magic consequences still occur, including forced minimap closure; ordinary regeneration rules then govern recovery.
rows.name: Mana Barrier

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, Magic-using AI
rows.effect: Replaces Mana Barrier and sets ManaBarrierFeatDiversionFraction = 0.30. This feat remains unavailable to Wizard-class actors. For eligible non-Wizards, HPToMagicDiversionFraction = 0.30. The same post-mitigation continuous calculation and 1 Magic per 1 prevented HP exchange apply; fractional HP diversion and fractional Magic damage are legal, diversion is limited by CurrentMagic, and any unpayable remainder is taken as HP damage normally.

The timer does not run and no regeneration occurs while the minimap or another regeneration-suppressing sustained effect remains active.
rows.name: Mana Spring

rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Grants exactly one additional voluntary jump per airborne cycle. After leaving authoritative ground, a fresh Space press while airborne may consume 5 Magic to perform one additional jump; if fewer than 5 Magic is available, no Cloud Step occurs and no partial cost is paid. The additional jump uses ordinary jump strength unless another compatible movement feat modifies voluntary jump height; Spring Heel therefore doubles both the ground jump and Cloud Step jump when both are owned. When Wall Jump is also owned, a fresh airborne Space press that has a valid unused Wall Jump resolves Wall Jump first and leaves Cloud Step unused; once the actor is no longer eligible for that wall jump, a later fresh Space press may still consume Cloud Step normally. Cloud Step and Wall Jump are separate once-per-airborne-cycle resources and may therefore both occur before the next legitimate ground contact. Cloud Step resets only after legitimate ground contact and cannot create repeated air jumps from wall contact, props, Push, or scripted movement. Canonical anti-top, gate, ceiling, and progression blockers remain authoritative.
rows.name: Cloud Step

rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Once per airborne cycle, the actor may hold Space at the apex of an eligible jump to enter a controllable float for up to 3.0 seconds. Float On spends Magic continuously at 5 Magic per second, so using the complete 3.0-second duration costs exactly 15 Magic; partial use costs only the proportional amount actually floated. The float ends immediately when Space is released, the 3.0-second cap is reached, available Magic is exhausted, or legitimate ground contact occurs. Floating suppresses ordinary downward acceleration enough to maintain the intended brief Princess-Peach-style hang time but does not create upward flight; ordinary horizontal air control remains available. Once Float On has been started or exhausted during an airborne cycle, it cannot be started again until legitimate ground contact resets it. Float On is always the lowest-priority Space behavior. A fresh airborne Space press that can legally trigger Wall Jump or Cloud Step resolves that discrete jump instead of starting Float. If Cloud Step is owned and still unused, Float On remains ineligible at an earlier apex; it may activate only after Cloud Step has actually been performed. When Wall Jump is also owned, Wall Jump may occur before or after Cloud Step according to wall proximity, and a later eligible apex may still start Float; merely owning an unused Wall Jump does not suppress Float when no valid wall is currently within WallJumpProbeDistance. This supports the canonical sequence ground jump -> Wall Jump when near a wall -> Cloud Step after moving clear -> hold Space at the later apex for Float, while also supporting ground jump -> Cloud Step -> Wall Jump -> Float if the actor reaches a wall later in the same airborne cycle. Without Cloud Step, Float On may activate at the apex of the ordinary ground jump or, if a Wall Jump was used afterward, at the later Wall Jump apex. Canonical anti-top, gate, ceiling, and progression blockers remain authoritative.
rows.name: Float On

rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Crouching gradually transforms the actor toward SizeShifterTargetScale = 0.33 over a full 3.0-second baseline-to-minimum transition; releasing crouch reverses the transformation toward that actor's ordinary non-Size-Shifter PlayerTargetScale at the same continuous rate, so partial transformations reverse smoothly rather than snapping or restarting a fresh timer. Size Shifter is a one-rank feat and costs no Magic. The third-person/world model, combat hurt volume, camera presentation where safe, and shared PushSizeScale track the current interpolated Size Shifter scale so a deeply shrunken actor is harder to hit but also easier to push and is pushed farther under the canonical size-based push rules. The authoritative movement/collision hull, stair legality, USE reach, weapon traces, gate permissions, and progression geometry never shrink below their ordinary crouched legal values, so Size Shifter cannot crawl through walls, locked gates, illegal gaps, or other geometry that the normal actor could not traverse. If Little Guy or Big Guy is also owned, that feat defines the actor's ordinary non-Size-Shifter return scale; Size Shifter still approaches an absolute 0.33 while crouched and returns toward that build's ordinary scale when crouch is released.
rows.name: Size Shifter

rows.effect: Each successful committed cast of BLAST, BEAM, BOMB, MISSILE, or BOLT schedules exactly one phantom echo 0.50 seconds later at no additional Magic cost. The server snapshots the original cast's launch origin, authoritative maze cell where applicable, launch orientation or initial vector, Form identity, selected Content damage type, and the caster-side Magic damage state needed to reproduce that attack. The echo originates from that exact captured launch point and initial direction, never from the caster's position 0.50 seconds later. It uses the original Form's geometry, collision rules, target budget, delivery behavior, selected Content damage type, WIS MagicPowerMultiplier, elemental damage resolution, Boom authority, and all other otherwise-applicable caster-side Magic damage modifiers, but reduces only the Form's authored base damage-die count according to AftershockDiceCount = max(1, floor(OriginalFormBaseDamageDiceCount / 2)). With the current Form catalog this yields Blast 1d6, Beam 1d6, Bomb 1d6, Missile 1d6, and Bolt 2d6 before ordinary scaling and Boom resolution. The echo is damage-only and carries no Content rider, status, control, Push, or other non-damage rider: Earth creates no Push; Fire no Immolated; Dark no Poisoned; Ice no Held; Light no Muted; Electric no Morale rider. Current target-side weakness, resistance, immunity, blockers, collision, and other ordinary Magic interactions are resolved when the phantom attack actually launches or lands. Aftershock never triggers from SUMMON, summoned-Seeker proxy attacks, another Aftershock echo, passive or scripted Magic, or a failed or cancelled cast, and an echo cannot recursively schedule another echo. A committed original cast still produces its scheduled echo if the caster moves afterward; only invalid session/level cleanup or cancellation before original cast commitment removes the pending echo. The phantom is a real second Form attack against then-current world state, not delayed guaranteed damage to the original targets. Its visual presentation reuses the Form effect at AftershockVisualAlpha = 0.50 × OriginalVisualAlpha and deterministically generates the complementary opposite color by rotating the original effect hue 180 degrees while preserving saturation and lightness/value as closely as renderer constraints allow; achromatic originals use a deterministic high-contrast complementary fallback. For steerable Missile, the echo begins from the captured original launch transform and thereafter retains ordinary Missile steering behavior; the other eligible Forms use their corresponding captured-origin semantics.
rows.name: Aftershock

The feat provides no benefit when lod_mapless or another authoritative state prevents the minimap from opening.

rows.effect: Immediately grants exactly one additional distinct Magic Form from the canonical six-Form catalog. The granted Form is selected deterministically from the Hero's currently unowned Forms using a dedicated grand_unified_theory RNG substream; the player does not choose it, and acquisition never rerolls because I is opened, closed, or revisited. The Form persists for that campaign exactly like a scheduled class-progression Form grant. Grand Unified Theory composes with the synchronized class milestone chart rather than replacing it: a Wizard who would normally own four Forms by Level 10 may reach five, while a Rogue or Fighter who would normally own two may reach three. The Content persists for that campaign exactly like a scheduled class-progression Content grant and may be attached to any owned compatible Magic Form through the ordinary shared Form/Content spellcasting authority. rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Adds a dedicated rebindable Polymorph action whose default keyboard binding is J. Activation is legal only while alive, player-controlled, not already polymorphed, and CurrentMagic = 100. Pressing the Polymorph action consumes the entire Magic pool immediately, sets CurrentMagic = 0, and transforms the actor into a chicken for PolymorphDurationSeconds = 4d6! seconds. Each of the four duration d6 chains uses the universal fixed natural-6 recursive explosion rule; these are timing dice rather than damage dice and therefore do not inherit Rogue damage-die mastery, DEX BoomShift, Wizard magical Boom rules, weapon-specific thresholds, or other damage-die modifiers. Minimum duration is 4 seconds, there is no fixed maximum, and expected duration is 16.8 seconds. Polymorph cannot be cancelled voluntarily once begun. While in chicken form, the actor is removed from ordinary hostile AI target-candidate selection and any AI target lock that exists only because that actor was a hostile target is cleared immediately; this is temporary target suppression, not a faction change, charm, invulnerability, or deletion from combat. AI may not deliberately reacquire or aim a new hostile attack at the chicken until the form ends. Attacks/projectiles already validly committed before transformation may finish resolving, and the chicken remains fully vulnerable to incidental line-of-fire hits, penetration, explosions, cones, persistent hazards, environmental damage, status damage, Reckless-friendly-fire geometry, and any other damage source that reaches it without requiring a new hostile target selection. Chicken form is a disengagement utility state: the actor cannot initiate weapon fire, melee attacks, damaging Magic, active spellcasting, or other attack-tagged actions while transformed. Tapping Space while airborne performs a chicken flap that adds another ordinary upward jump impulse; there is no per-airborne-cycle flap count while Polymorph remains active, so repeated taps create the intended comic chicken flight. Canonical ceilings, anti-container-top blockers, locked gates, progression barriers, map bounds, and other topology protections remain authoritative, so repeated flapping can aid escape and vertical maneuvering but can never fly over or through forbidden progression geometry. The world model becomes a readable chicken presentation and emits intermittent spatialized chicken clucks/boks during the transformation; audiovisual presentation must not obscure combat information. When PolymorphDurationSeconds expires, the actor automatically returns to their ordinary character form and normal hostile-target eligibility. Magic regeneration remains suppressed for PolymorphPostRecoveryDelaySeconds = 5.0 after reversion; after that delay, ordinary INT-scaled Magic regeneration rules resume. Because a new Polymorph requires CurrentMagic = 100 again, the full-pool requirement plus forced zeroing and post-form regeneration delay provide the feat's effective cooldown without a second independent cooldown timer.
rows.name: Polymorph

rows.effect: While the actor is voluntarily moving with backward movement input, BackpedalMovementMultiplier = 1.25. Backpedaling is true whenever the actor has nonzero voluntary horizontal movement input and their signed forward/back movement input is negative relative to their current facing; holding S alone or together with lateral movement therefore qualifies, while pure strafing, forward movement, knockback, Push, sliding, falling, and other forced movement do not. Apply BackpedalMovementMultiplier to the actor's resolved voluntary locomotion speed after ordinary walk/run/sprint mode, DEX movement scaling, and other compatible ordinary movement modifiers. It does not replace or disable normal sprint. If Haste is active, Haste applies normally to the already backpedal-modified legal locomotion speed, so the two feats compose multiplicatively rather than through a separate movement authority. The feat changes no forward-only movement, pure lateral movement, jump velocity, Wall Jump, Cloud Step, Float On, projectile motion, or forced movement.

Pressing H while alive, player-controlled, and at positive Magic toggles Haste ON; pressing H again toggles it OFF. While Haste is ON and funded, HasteMovementMultiplier = 2.00 and applies to the actor's resolved voluntary locomotion speed after ordinary walk/run/sprint mode, DEX movement scaling, MapOpenMovementMultiplier when applicable, and other compatible ordinary movement modifiers. HasteMagicDrainRate = CurrentMapOpenMagicDrainRate, using the same personal WIS-scaled utility-Magic rate as map viewing. Magic regeneration is suppressed while Haste is actively draining. Haste and map viewing are independent sustained Magic consumers: at base Haste, if both are active simultaneously, TotalUtilityMagicDrainRate = CurrentMapOpenMagicDrainRate + HasteMagicDrainRate = 2 × CurrentMapOpenMagicDrainRate. Reaching 0 Magic immediately turns Haste OFF and returns locomotion to its ordinary legal speed; death or loss of player control likewise ends the active Haste state. A map force-close caused by damage or map-Magic exhaustion ends only the map state and its map-open movement bonus; it does not itself toggle Haste OFF if Haste still has positive Magic. Haste changes no jump velocity, Wall Jump, Cloud Step, Float On, Push/knockback, falling, projectile motion, or forced movement.

rows.name: Cartographer

rows.actors: Heroes and human Soldiers with minimap access
rows.effect: After the normal WIS UtilityMagicCostMultiplier is calculated, minimap drain is multiplied by an additional 0.85, with final MapDrainPerSecond never lower than 3.0 Magic/second. Magic regeneration remains completely disabled while the map is open.
rows.name: Frugal Cartography

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: Grants MagicalDamageReduction = max(0, WIS_MOD). Whenever this actor receives an incoming damage event tagged magical=true from any source, reduce that event's aggregated magical damage by MagicalDamageReduction after ordinary damage dice/Boom resolution, CON DamageResistancePerDie, source-side scaling, and elemental/identity modifiers, but before Arcane Shield HP-to-Magic diversion, lethal intercepts, and final HP loss. Apply True Faith exactly once per resolved damage event, never once per die, pellet, Boom continuation, or internal sub-hit, and never reduce damage below 0. Physical-only events with magical=false receive no reduction. If an unusual event is tagged both physical=true and magical=true, it qualifies because it is still an explicitly magical damage source. True Faith does not alter MagicSave, Arcane Integrity, elemental resistance/weakness, status saves, Magic cost, or any non-damage effect.
rows.name: True Faith

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: While this feat is ready, the first incoming damage event tagged physical=true automatically receives PhysicalDamageReduction = max(0, WIS_MOD), applied once to the event's aggregated physical damage after ordinary damage dice/Boom resolution, CON DamageResistancePerDie, source-side scaling, and elemental/identity modifiers, but before Arcane Shield HP-to-Magic diversion, lethal intercepts, and final HP loss. Never reduce damage below 0. After an eligible physical event consumes the ready state, roll MindOverMatterCooldownSeconds = 3d4 seconds and do not apply Mind Over Matter again until that cooldown expires. These three d4 timing dice are sealed, non-damage utility dice and never explode or inherit Rogue damage-die mastery, DEX BoomShift, Wizard magical Boom rules, weapon-specific explosion rules, or other attack-die modifiers. When the cooldown expires, Mind Over Matter becomes ready again. Magical-only events with physical=false do not consume the ready state. A mixed physical=true/magical=true event may receive True Faith's magical reduction and, when Mind Over Matter is ready, Mind Over Matter's physical reduction on the same resolved event; each applies once and final damage is clamped at 0. Mind Over Matter does not alter Push, wall-slam damage, hit-stun, status saves, MagicSave, or any non-damage physical effect.
rows.name: Mind Over Matter

rows.actors: Player-controlled Heroes only
rows.effect: Adds a private old-school synthetic GPS navigation assist with a dedicated rebindable toggle whose default keyboard binding is G. GPS starts enabled immediately when the feat is acquired. Acquisition displays a concise tooltip/system notice: GPS ENABLED — If it gets annoying, press G to turn it off. Press G again to turn it back on. Pressing the GPS action toggles the feature without spending Magic; every toggle plays a short electronic switch/chime and produces the ordinary bounded on-screen system notice GPS ON or GPS OFF. While enabled, GPS becomes eligible once the Hero remains in the same canonical maze cell without meaningful locomotion for GPSIdleDelaySeconds = 3 + 1d6 seconds. The d6 is a sealed non-damage utility die and never explodes or inherits attack-die modifiers. Aim/facing may change while stationary. GPS speaks at most one guidance bark per stationary episode; meaningful locomotion re-arms it, so remaining still does not cause repeated chatter. When triggered, GPS reads only the authoritative canonical route from the Hero's current cell to the currently active progression objective and emits one short 2000s/early-2010s-style direction assembled from a small fixed synthetic/concatenative voice bank. Supported phrase families include TURN LEFT, TURN RIGHT, TURN AROUND, CONTINUE FORWARD, IN N SQUARES TURN LEFT/RIGHT, IN N SQUARES TAKE THE STAIRS UP/DOWN, TAKE THE STAIRS UP/DOWN, and YOU HAVE ARRIVED AT YOUR DESTINATION. N is derived from the contiguous legal route segment to the next turn, stair transition, or objective rather than guessed. GPS never invents a shortcut, predicts future progression stages, reveals enemies or loot, or performs a second pathfinding authority: it consumes the same canonical current-objective route used by ordinary navigation/breadcrumb logic. GPS is supplemental information and remains available even when lod_mapless 1 removes the visual minimap; it does not itself reveal a map or persistent route display. Active combat, death/spectating, staging, cutscenes, and other states where a navigation bark would be intrusive suspend the idle trigger. GPS has no Magic cost and does not alter Magic regeneration, BreadcrumbCells, movement, combat statistics, rewards, or objective logic.
rows.name: GPS

rows.actors: Cooperative Heroes with at least one Magic Form unlocked
rows.effect: Adds AstralReachBonusCells = 2 to the shared Magic Form spatial-scaling authority. This flat +2-cell bonus layers on top of the caster's ordinary MagicSpatialBonusCells = max(1, WIS_MOD); it does not replace Wisdom scaling or create a second range algorithm. The +2 applies only to each Form dimension already marked Wisdom-scaled: Blast gains +2 cells of graph reach; Beam gains +2 cells of linear reach; Bomb keeps fixed throw range but gains +2 cells of explosion radius; Missile gains +2 cells of guided-flight range and +2 cells of explosion radius; Bolt gains +2 cells of projectile reach. Future Magic Forms inherit the same semantic rule automatically: Astral Reach adds +2 cells to each spatial dimension the core Wisdom authority marks scalable and does nothing to dimensions the Form keeps static. Existing geometry, obstruction, target-once, penetration, and attack-work rules remain unchanged. Astral Reach changes no damage dice, Magic cost, Boom rules, Content surcharge/riders, Push, status behavior, projectile speed, steering responsiveness, minimap range, BreadcrumbCells, GPS, Force Shout, or any non-Form system.
rows.name: Astral Reach

rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Warns about visible hostile monsters behind you and directly to either side. RearRangeCells = max(1, WIS_MOD), without Astral Reach. Quantize horizontal facing to the nearest cardinal maze direction. The rear footprint remains three cells wide for depths 1 through RearRangeCells: directly behind, plus one cell on either side of each rear cell. Add a single-cell-wide ray directly left and directly right from the player's current cell, each extending SideRangeCells = ceil(RearRangeCells / 2). No forward cells or other floors qualify. Closed walls, closed gates and ordinary blocking geometry still block detection. Retain the selected monster while it qualifies; otherwise choose by shortest footprint depth, then smallest absolute lateral offset, then stable actor identity. On acquisition or replacement after the prior selection ceases to qualify, name the monster in a private BEHIND YOU, LEFT or RIGHT notice in the live die-readout and Die Log, play a clearly audible alert, and briefly show a violet directional light toward its position at detection. The light is a transient directional notification, not an enemy outline, minimap marker or persistent tracker. Do not repeat the alert while the same selected monster remains qualified. No target lock, aim assist, combat bonus, through-wall detection or AI behavior change.
rows.name: Spatial Awareness

rows.actors: Heroes and human Soldiers
rows.effect: While controlled by a human and wielding an equipped damage-dealing weapon, Killer Instinct remains dormant unless at least two living hostile actors are simultaneously inside the player's ordinary forward view and pass the same player-facing visibility/line-of-sight authority used for legal target identification. When that multi-hostile condition first becomes true and remains continuously true for 0.50 seconds, perform one target-priority evaluation; while it remains true, reevaluate no more than once every 1.00 second. If fewer than two valid hostiles remain, immediately clear the highlight and stop all Killer Instinct evaluation until the condition becomes true again; there is no general per-frame Think scan. Candidate discovery must reuse the existing visible/targetable hostile set or equivalent cached authority and may not iterate every world entity solely for this feat. For each valid candidate, compute a cheap deterministic EstimatedEffectiveDamagePerShot for one ordinary primary-fire trigger pull from the equipped weapon's current authored attack profile, using current deterministic attacker/target modifiers and mean damage-die values; do not roll dice, simulate Boom chains, predict future status procs, or Monte Carlo attacks. EstimatedShotsToKill = max(1, ceil(CurrentHP / max(1, EstimatedEffectiveDamagePerShot))). If one or more candidates have EstimatedShotsToKill = 1, select the one with the greatest EstimatedEffectiveDamagePerShot - CurrentHP kill margin; otherwise select the candidate with the lowest EstimatedShotsToKill. Break any remaining tie by lower CurrentHP, then stable actor ID. Render one red outline/halo tightly around the selected hostile model. The outline is informational only: it grants no aim assist, targeting lock, damage, AI-priority change, extra detection range, through-wall awareness, or tracking after ordinary visibility is lost, and it clears immediately when the target dies or becomes invalid.
rows.name: Killer Instinct

rows.actors: Heroes and human Soldiers
rows.effect: While controlled by a human, whenever this actor directly looks at a monster through the canonical look-at/target-identification trace, render an Omniscience readout above that monster at the same presentation anchor used for player identity text. For an ordinary AI monster, the readout shows the monster's canonical type/archetype name, current Combat Level, current class, and current Hit Points as CurrentHP/MaxHP. Example structure: Soldier • Level 21 • Fighter • HP 84/117. The values update live while the target remains valid. Omniscience is informational only: it grants no extra targeting range, no through-wall or off-screen awareness, no outline or tracking after look-away, and no combat/stat bonus. A human-controlled Soldier is still a monster for Omniscience purposes, but its existing HumanSoldierText remains the primary identity line; Omniscience appends the same Type/Level/Class/HP readout rather than replacing or hiding the controlling player's identity. Non-monster world entities and cooperative Heroes do not receive this monster-stat readout.
rows.name: Omniscience

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: Adds +2 to MagicSave against explicitly resistible magical effects.
rows.name: Spellward

rows.actors: Cooperative heroes
rows.effect: Sixth Sense grants three personal perception effects. First, the owner can visually perceive any entity whose authoritative state includes invisible=true. Invisibility is a reusable shared entity-state primitive rather than a Watcher-specific exception: Watchers use it now, and future enemies, effects, or actors may use the same state. An invisible entity is rendered only for the owning client as a clearly readable translucent silhouette/outline at its true current world position whenever that entity would otherwise satisfy ordinary world visibility and line-of-sight rules if invisibility were ignored. Second, Sixth Sense grants Nearby Hostile Sense: every living hostile entity on the owner's current floor whose cell-coordinate distance is within 2 grid cells is rendered to that owner as a readable through-geometry outline even when intervening walls or props block line of sight. For this sensor, NearbyCellDistance = max(abs(enemyCellX-ownerCellX), abs(enemyCellY-ownerCellY)); the effect applies when NearbyCellDistance <= 2 and floorId matches. This local 5x5-cell neighborhood intentionally ignores wall connectivity and closed-gate edges for perception only. Invisible hostiles within that neighborhood are also revealed by the same outline. Third, Sixth Sense grants Watcher Motion Sense: whenever a living Watcher is in its authoritative moving/locomotion state, each Sixth Sense owner on the same floor receives a private 3D positional Watcher movement sound attached to that Watcher's true current position. This cue plays whether the Watcher is visible or invisible and does not require line of sight; ordinary spatial attenuation provides direction and proximity, so a distant Watcher does not become an all-floor audio beacon. The cue starts when authoritative Watcher locomotion begins and stops when locomotion stops, the Watcher dies/despawns, the player changes floor, or Sixth Sense is no longer active. The movement sound is transmitted/rendered only for eligible Sixth Sense owners; players without the feat receive no such sound event. These effects create no minimap marker, breadcrumb, directional arrow, nameplate through the world, aim assistance, target lock, ballistic permission through geometry, AI aggro knowledge, or interaction permission. Sixth Sense never changes an entity's invisible state, cloak duration, AI/state machine, collision, targetability rules, or visibility to any other player; players without the feat perceive the entity normally. The server authoritatively determines feat ownership, invisible state, hostility, floor, cell coordinates, and Watcher locomotion state; owning clients render only authorized silhouettes and private Watcher movement audio. FeatDirector may offer Sixth Sense whenever the actor is a cooperative hero who meets WIS 12; Watchers or any other invisibility-using enemy need not currently be present because the 2-cell hostile-sense effect is independently useful.
rows.name: Sixth Sense

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: Replaces Spellward's +2 with +4 total MagicSave. It does not invent a save against pure weapon damage or effects that are authored as unresistible.
rows.name: Spellbreaker

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: Replaces Spellbreaker's +4 with +6 total MagicSave against explicitly resistible magical effects. It never creates a save where the authored effect supplies none and never overrides explicit boss/elite immunity or unresistible-effect tags.
rows.name: Spellbane

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with a Magic push
rows.effect: Actor-authored magic_push displacement is multiplied by 1.25. Force Shout is the initial intended beneficiary. Physical-push feats do not automatically stack unless a cross-system bridge makes the event eligible for both families.
rows.name: Force Multiplier

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, eligible AI
rows.effect: When the actor's Magic attack exploits an elemental weakness, roll the weakness-bonus table twice and keep the more favorable bonus. This affects the weakness damage roll only and does not duplicate the hit, stun, knockback, or Magic cost.
rows.name: Attunement
rows.prerequisite: Elemental system active and actor owns an elemental Magic attack

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with an eligible hit-stun source
rows.effect: After the normal ChaHitStunInflictMultiplier is calculated, multiply eligible hit stun inflicted by this actor by 1.10. This applies once per resolved target hit/event, not once per pellet or sub-hit, and remains subject to the ordinary retrigger guard, resistance, anti-stunlock rules, and hard caps. This is separate from the Menacing intimidation family: Unnerving Presence improves hit-stun pressure, while Menacing/Dreadful/Terrifying improve Morale pressure.
rows.name: Unnerving Presence

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with an eligible hit-stun source
rows.effect: Replaces Unnerving Presence's feat multiplier with 1.20 total. It stacks multiplicatively with the continuous CHA-derived hit-stun multiplier but does not create hit stun on attacks that normally have none.
rows.name: Dazing Presence

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with an eligible hit-stun source
rows.effect: Replaces the lower-rank feat multiplier with 1.30 total. Weapon-specific and weakness multipliers still resolve afterward, and all anti-stunlock/retrigger/cap safeguards remain authoritative.
rows.name: Overwhelming Presence

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI actors subject to Morale
rows.effect: Adds +2 to MoraleSave when this actor is the defender in an eligible Morale check. This defensive family is controller-agnostic: for AI it helps resist Morale Flee, while for human-controlled actors it helps resist the brief Intimidated state caused by a qualifying massive hit.
rows.name: Iron Nerve

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI actors subject to Morale
rows.effect: Replaces Iron Nerve and adds +4 total to MoraleSave. It changes courage only and does not grant immunity to Morale, remove a legal trauma trigger, or shorten an already-running fear/intimidation state unless another rule explicitly says so.
rows.name: Unbreakable Nerve

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: This is rank 1 of the dedicated offensive intimidation family. Adds +2 to MoraleDC whenever this actor is the credited attacker for a Morale check. AI actors may acquire this family through the same ordinary deterministic FeatDirector eligibility and selection rules as other AI-legal feats whenever their CHA and prerequisites qualify; it is not reserved for player characters. Against a human-controlled defender, also set HumanMoraleTraumaFraction = 0.30 for damage credited to this actor, so a single hit dealing more than 30% of current MaxHP may trigger Morale instead of the ordinary greater-than-one-third requirement. This never enables the below-50%-HP trigger or repeated-below-half trigger against humans. Against AI defenders, trigger cadence remains the ordinary AI Morale cadence; Menacing improves the opposed check rather than creating extra checks.
rows.name: Menacing

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: Replaces Menacing's +2 with +4 total MoraleDC. Against human-controlled defenders, replaces Menacing's trauma threshold with HumanMoraleTraumaFraction = 0.25, so a single hit dealing more than 25% of current MaxHP may trigger Morale. It still never enables a human below-50%-HP or repeated-below-half trigger. Dreadful replaces rather than stacks with Menacing's threshold and DC bonus.
rows.name: Dreadful

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: Retains Dreadful's +4 total MoraleDC. Against human-controlled defenders, replaces Dreadful's trauma threshold with HumanMoraleTraumaFraction = 0.20, so a single hit dealing more than 20% of current MaxHP may trigger Morale; it still never enables the below-50%-HP or repeated-below-half trigger against humans. In addition, the first Morale Save each eligible defender makes against this actor during an encounter is rolled twice and the lower natural d20 is kept before modifiers. Later Morale Saves by that defender against the same actor return to one d20. Terrifying therefore specializes an actor into intimidation by widening the set of genuinely traumatic hits against human-controlled targets and making its first fear attempt especially difficult, while the defender's controller-based Morale cooldown remains unchanged and continues to prevent repeated player lockout.
rows.name: Terrifying

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Sets IntimidationProcChance = 0.11. If an eligible target-hit event damages a surviving defender whose MoraleCheckCooldown is inactive and that same event did not already require a Morale check from an ordinary trauma trigger, a successful proc forces exactly one Morale check even when the hit would otherwise be below the defender's trauma threshold. The ordinary attacker-CHA MoraleDC and defender-CHA MoraleSave formulas apply, and the normal controller-specific cooldown begins after that check whether it succeeds or fails.
rows.name: Daunting

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Daunting and sets IntimidationProcChance = 0.22. All one-check-per-damage-event, Morale cooldown, controller-specific failure, and anti-player-lockout rules remain unchanged.
rows.name: Cowing

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Cowing and sets IntimidationProcChance = 0.33. All other Daunting-family semantics remain unchanged. Menacing→Dreadful→Terrifying is a separate complementary family: its MoraleDC bonuses, human trauma-threshold reductions, and Terrifying first-save disadvantage apply normally to Morale checks forced by this proc family, allowing deliberate investment in both frequency and potency without duplicate proc rolls.
rows.name: Overawing

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: When an enemy fails a Morale Save against this actor, every other eligible AI hostile below 50% MaxHP within 2 graph cells may immediately make one Morale check against the same actor. A secondary failure does not recursively trigger another cascade, and each potential secondary target has a 3.0-second cascade-immunity timer.
rows.name: Panic Is Contagious

rows.actors: AI Watchers and human-controlled Soldiers only
rows.effect: After normal CHA SpotSystem formulas, add +1 SpotTargetRangeCells, +1 SpotDrawRangeCells, and +2 SpotMarkDurationSeconds, still respecting the global SpotSystem clamps and same-floor rule.
rows.name: Point It Out

rows.actors: AI Watchers and human-controlled Soldiers only
rows.effect: Replaces the prior spotting bonus with +2 target-range cells, +2 draw-radius cells, and +4 mark-duration seconds total, subject to clamps and same-floor restrictions.
rows.name: Rally the Hunt

rows.actors: AI Watchers and human-controlled Soldiers only
rows.effect: Replaces the prior spotting bonus with +3 target-range cells, +3 draw-radius cells, and +6 mark-duration seconds total, subject to clamps and same-floor restrictions.
rows.name: Command the Hunt

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI
rows.effect: Rank 1 of the passive personality-aura family. While this actor is alive, roll a sealed non-exploding 3d4-second AuraPulseInterval; when it expires, every living hostile actor whose authoritative canonical maze-cell identity is the same cell as this actor takes PersonalityAuraDamage = max(0, CHA_MOD) flat untyped passive damage. After the pulse resolves, immediately roll a fresh sealed 3d4-second interval and repeat while the owner remains alive. The three timing d4s are utility dice and never explode or inherit BoomShift, Rogue die mastery, Wizard magical Boom rules, or other damage-die modifiers. PersonalityAuraDamage is not an attack, not physical, and not magical; it has no damage dice and therefore receives no per-die CON resistance. It is FeedbackIneligible=true, MoraleIneligible=true, StatusProcIneligible=true, and cannot trigger Bloodletter, Aggressive Personality, Self-Actualization, hit-stun, Push, wall-slam, or any other effect requiring an attributable offensive hit. Ordinary lethal handling and kill attribution still apply. Rank 1 affects only hostiles occupying the owner's own canonical cell at the instant of the pulse.
rows.name: Abrasive Personality

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI
rows.effect: Replaces Abrasive Personality's radius while retaining the same max(0, CHA_MOD) flat damage, sealed 3d4-second rerolled pulse interval, and passive-damage exclusions. Set PersonalityAuraCellRadius = 1. At each pulse, affect every living hostile on the same canonical floor whose cell lies in the 3x3 grid neighborhood centered on the owner: the owner's own cell plus every cell that touches it by an edge or corner. Equivalently, for canonical same-floor row/column coordinates, max(abs(TargetRow-OwnerRow), abs(TargetColumn-OwnerColumn)) <= 1. The radius is cell-based rather than a raw world-unit sphere.
rows.name: Narcissism

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI
rows.effect: Replaces Narcissism's radius while retaining the same max(0, CHA_MOD) flat damage, sealed 3d4-second rerolled pulse interval, and passive-damage exclusions. Set PersonalityAuraCellRadius = 2. At each pulse, affect every living hostile on the same canonical floor within the 5x5 grid neighborhood centered on the owner: the owner's cell, every cell touching it, and every cell touching any of those cells out to two grid spaces. Equivalently, max(abs(TargetRow-OwnerRow), abs(TargetColumn-OwnerColumn)) <= 2. Higher ranks replace rather than stack with lower ranks, so one owner produces exactly one personality-aura pulse stream regardless of rank.
rows.name: Megalomania

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one discrete active Magic activation
rows.effect: Rank 1 of the triggered Magic-aura family. Whenever this actor successfully initiates a discrete active Magic use that actually spends Magic, resolve exactly one AuraBurst pulse centered on the actor as an add-on to that Magic activation. AuraBurstDamage = max(0, CHA_MOD) flat magical aura damage to every living hostile actor whose authoritative canonical maze-cell identity is the same cell as the owner at the instant the Magic use begins. The burst is a separate supplemental damage event rather than additional damage dice on the triggering spell or ability; it does not inherit that Magic use's Form, Content, element, damage dice, Boom behavior, rider, targeting, or status effects. AuraBurstDamage has no damage dice and therefore receives no per-die CON resistance. It is magical=true but is not itself an active Magic activation, cannot recursively trigger Aura Burst, and is ineligible for Self-Actualization, ordinary offensive status procs, Bloodletter, hit-stun, Push, wall-slam, Feedback, or Morale. Ordinary magical-damage defenses such as True Faith may reduce it. Continuous or maintenance Magic drains, including map viewing, Haste, Float On, Arcane Shield diversion, passive regeneration, and other resource-over-time accounting, do not generate repeated bursts. Rank 1 affects only hostiles occupying the owner's own canonical cell.
rows.name: Aura Burst

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one discrete active Magic activation
rows.effect: Replaces Aura Burst's radius while retaining the same one-pulse-per-discrete-Magic-activation trigger, max(0, CHA_MOD) flat magical AuraBurstDamage, and triggered-aura exclusions. Set AuraBurstCellRadius = 1. Each qualifying Magic activation affects every living hostile on the same canonical floor whose cell lies in the 3x3 grid neighborhood centered on the owner: the owner's own cell plus every cell touching it by an edge or corner. Equivalently, for canonical same-floor row/column coordinates, max(abs(TargetRow-OwnerRow), abs(TargetColumn-OwnerColumn)) <= 1. The radius is cell-based rather than a raw world-unit sphere.
rows.name: Radiance

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one discrete active Magic activation
rows.effect: Replaces Radiance's radius while retaining the same one-pulse-per-discrete-Magic-activation trigger, max(0, CHA_MOD) flat magical AuraBurstDamage, and triggered-aura exclusions. Set AuraBurstCellRadius = 2. Each qualifying Magic activation affects every living hostile on the same canonical floor within the 5x5 grid neighborhood centered on the owner: the owner's cell, every cell touching it, and every cell touching any of those cells out to two grid spaces. Equivalently, max(abs(TargetRow-OwnerRow), abs(TargetColumn-OwnerColumn)) <= 2. Higher ranks replace rather than stack with lower Aura Burst ranks, so one Magic activation produces exactly one AuraBurst pulse regardless of owned rank. Aura Burst/Radiance/Majesty and Abrasive Personality/Narcissism/Megalomania are independent feat families: an actor may own both, their eligibility and timers/triggers remain separate, and when both legitimately resolve against the same target their damage events both apply rather than one suppressing or replacing the other.
rows.name: Majesty

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with a canonical Magic pool and passive Magic regeneration
rows.effect: Adds the owner's positive Charisma modifier to the same canonical passive Magic-regeneration calculation that normally uses Intelligence. Set AcademicRegenCHAContribution = max(0, CHA_MOD) and EffectiveMagicRegenModifier = INT_MOD + AcademicRegenCHAContribution, then compute MagicRegenMultiplier = clamp(1 + 0.10 × EffectiveMagicRegenModifier, 0.50, 2.00). This is cumulative with the ordinary INT contribution rather than replacing it. Academic Achievement changes only passive Magic regeneration speed: it does not enable regeneration while the canonical Magic system says regeneration is suspended, does not increase Max Magic, does not alter active Magic costs, map drain, spell damage, MagicSave, or any other INT/CHA rule, and cannot regenerate above the actor's ordinary Magic maximum.
rows.name: Academic Achievement

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one eligible magical attack
rows.effect: Adds a flat outgoing damage bonus equal to max(0, CHA_MOD) to each eligible attributable magical attack or active damaging Magic event initiated by this actor. Apply the bonus exactly once per resolved target damage event after ordinary source-side damage multipliers; it does not alter die count, die size, Boom qualification, continuation generation, status-application chance, or Magic cost. Multi-target Magic may receive the bonus once for each genuinely damaged target, but individual damage dice, Boom continuations, pellets, cosmetic sub-hits, and other internal subcomponents never multiply it. Feedback, PoisonStepDamage, BleedTickDamage, ImmolatedDamage, environmental damage, reflected/reactive damage, and other non-attack or status-damage events are ineligible. Eligibility tests magical=true independently of any physical tag. A mixed physical=true/magical=true attack receives Self-Actualization and may also receive Aggressive Personality if the actor owns both feats, with each feat contributing its flat bonus once to the same resolved damage event.
rows.name: Self-Actualization

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one eligible physical attack
rows.effect: Aggressive Personality has a ready/cooldown state. While ready, the next eligible attributable physical attack activation that produces at least one physical=true damage event may add a flat outgoing damage bonus equal to max(0, CHA_MOD) to each eligible resolved target damage event created by that same originating attack, regardless of whether those events are also tagged magical=true. Apply the bonus exactly once per legitimately damaged target event after ordinary source-side damage multipliers; it does not alter damage dice, Boom qualification, push distance, wall-slam dice, status-proc chances, or other rider mechanics. After that originating attack finishes resolving and the bonus has applied at least once, consume the ready state and roll AggressivePersonalityCooldownSeconds = 1d3 seconds. This cooldown d3 is a sealed non-damage utility die and never explodes or inherits Rogue die mastery, BoomShift, Wizard magical Boom rules, weapon-specific explosion rules, or other attack-die modifiers. While the cooldown is active, Aggressive Personality contributes no CHA damage and qualifying attacks do not restart, extend, or reroll the cooldown. When the cooldown expires, the feat becomes ready again. A Shotgun shell or other single authored multi-target attack checks readiness once for the originating attack and, when ready, may grant the bonus once per damaged target after ordinary aggregation; pellets or internal sub-hits never consume separate cooldowns. Each genuinely separate bullet or authored projectile fired as a separate attack activation must find the feat ready on its own. Push-only effects, wall-slam/crush damage, Feedback, status damage, environmental damage, and other non-attack or reactive damage are ineligible and do not consume readiness. A mixed physical=true/magical=true event remains eligible for Aggressive Personality and may also receive Self-Actualization if the actor owns both feats; the two independently satisfied damage-class predicates may therefore both contribute once. If Aggressive Personality is on cooldown, it contributes no CHA-derived damage for Glow Up or any other effect that keys off an actual CHA_MOD damage contribution.
rows.name: Aggressive Personality

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI using ordinary feat eligibility
rows.effect: On acquisition, permanently increase the actor's intrinsic CHA score by +1, subject to the ordinary permanent ability-score ceiling. This is a real CHA increase and therefore immediately participates in all ordinary CHA-derived calculations. For the sole purpose of checking the printed ability-score prerequisite of an INT feat, EffectiveINTFeatQualificationScore = max(INT, CHA), using the actor's current CHA after this +1 increase. Winning Personality does not change the actor's actual INT score or INT_MOD and never substitutes CHA for INT in gameplay formulas, Magic regeneration, Arcane Break or Arcane Integrity contests, Wizard class mechanics, feat-effect scaling, or any other INT-derived mechanic. All non-ability prerequisites and restrictions remain fully authoritative, including prerequisite feats, class exclusions, controller/weapon access, and ordinary feat availability. The substituted qualification score also applies when constructing legal feat-draft or AI FeatDirector candidate pools, so an INT feat unlocked by Winning Personality may appear through the ordinary selection process. The permanent +1 CHA remains useful even if the actor never selects or uses an INT feat through Winning Personality.
rows.name: Winning Personality

rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes/human Soldiers with Crowbar-family access
rows.effect: Once per airborne cycle, a Crowbar-family hit made after consuming Cloud Step's feat-granted second jump and before legitimate ground contact adds one extra 1d6 physical-damage chain and doubles that hit's Crowbar-origin push distance before other compatible push multipliers. The bonus d6 obeys the universal exploding rule. Missing the swing does not consume the once-per-airborne-cycle strike; landing resets it.
rows.name: Meteor Strike

rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers
rows.effect: While Little Guy is active, MoraleDC gains an additional +2 against enemies within 2 graph cells of the actor. This stacks with the Menacing family but applies only at close range.
rows.name: Tiny Terror

rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers
rows.effect: When this actor deals melee damage or a physical push/wall-crush event, that event's MoraleDC gains an additional +2. It stacks with the Menacing family and exists specifically to make an intimidating giant bruiser build possible without changing ordinary ranged intimidation.
rows.name: Big Scary

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with physical push
rows.effect: A wall crush caused by this actor immediately requests a Morale check from the crushed target if it is otherwise morale-eligible, even if its normal one-second Morale recheck gate has not elapsed. This special request has a 3.0-second per-target cooldown. Other morale eligibility, immunity, and flee rules remain unchanged.
rows.name: Crash the Party

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, Magic-using AI
rows.effect: Actor-owned non-Magic damage Boomchains may now feed Magic: every second continuation die generated by the same non-Magic attack restores 1 Magic, up to 5 Magic per attack event. This does not alter explosion thresholds and never raises Magic above 100.
rows.name: Boom Battery

rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, eligible AI
rows.effect: The actor's Magic-origin pushes are additionally eligible for Pusher/Shover/Space Hog processing as already-pushing events. Force Multiplier resolves first; then, only when that attacker-target pair is not inside the shared 0.50-second PusherProcTargetCooldown, the Pusher-family proc may add its +168-world-unit physical displacement on success, and any resulting valid wall slam uses the actor's active Pusher-family wall-slam die. Force of Will does not make non-pushing Magic damage eligible for a Pusher proc. This is an explicit bridge feat; without it the physical-weapon Pusher family and magic_push family remain separate.
rows.name: Force of Will

rows.actors: Heroes and human Soldiers
rows.effect: Once per attack event, if a Luck-Ring reroll changes a non-exploding natural die result into an exploding kept result, refund 5 Magic after that die's reroll cost is paid. Continuation dice and later rerolls proceed normally; the refund can occur only once per attack event.
rows.name: Lucky Break
